question: Your agent upgrades a shared logging library across 40 repositories in one run. When a build breaks in a way that it cannot fix safely, it pauses and sends a handoff to the platform on-call engineer, who cannot see the agent's transcript. Each handoff states a clear root cause and a recommended action. However, the on-call engineer often cannot tell which repository and branch a handoff refers to. Which change best fixes this problem?

options.text: Add required fields for the repository and the branch to each handoff, next to the existing root cause and recommended action.
options.reason: A structured handoff protocol carries the identifying details of the case together with the root cause and recommended action. Adding the missing identifiers fixes the gap and keeps the useful content.

options.text: Attach the agent's full transcript to each handoff, so the on-call engineer can search the conversation for the repository and branch that failed.
options.reason: The guide calls for a compiled structured summary for recipients who lack the transcript. A raw transcript makes the on-call engineer dig for details that a summary field would state directly.

options.text: Have the agent keep retrying each broken build with new fixes until the build passes, so that it never needs to hand off to the on-call engineer mid-process.
options.reason: Cases that the agent cannot fix safely still need mid-process escalation. Avoiding the handoff does not fix the missing details in it.

options.text: Remove the recommended action from the handoff, so the on-call engineer reaches an independent judgment from the root cause and the build log.
options.reason: The recommended action is part of the structured handoff protocol. Removing it discards useful findings and does nothing about the missing repository and branch.
